summary: Susan L. Beningson specializes in Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr., attested in 2009.

Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at UCLA (~1969–1972). She served as a professor (~1971) and later Distinguished University Professor, Emerita, at Ohio State University.
Susan Meinheit is a Tibetology scholar whose career includes posts at the Library of Congress, attested in 1998 and 2007.

Susan Naquin is a historian and Sinologist who studied at Stanford (BA ~1962–1966) and Yale (MA ~1966–1968; PhD ~1968–1974). She taught at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and served as a professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at the Free University of Berlin and earned her PhD at Harvard. She taught at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and became Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who held a post as a colleague in the religion department at Amherst College around 1978.

Susan Whitfield is an archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Sinology scholar who earned her PhD from SOAS (1995). She directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and is a professor at the University of East Anglia.

Susannah Deane works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After degrees at Bangor, Bristol, and Cardiff (PhD 2010–2015), she held a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowship at Bristol (2017–2021) and a research post at the University of the West of England (2023).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a political scientist and Indologist educated at Sarah Lawrence, Harvard, and Radcliffe (PhD ~1951–1955). She taught at Harvard (~1954–1963) and the University of Chicago from 1964, and served as APSA president (2003–2004).
Susanne Kerekes is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania. She has held a post at Trinity College, Hartford.

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, and Stephanie W. Jamison. She held posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied and lectured (1986) at Visva-Bharati University. Sen also served as a lecturer in Indian religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist educated at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS (DLitt ~1919–1921), and University of Bonn. He held professorships at the University of Dhaka (~1923–1947) and Jadavpur University (1947).
Susmita Basu Majumdar is an archaeologist and Indologist. She was educated at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she later held an academic post.

Susumu Kajiura is a scholar of Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and as humanities lab director at the Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property, attested in 2001.

Susumu Otake is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied under Makio Takemura at the University of Tsukuba. He has held lecturer posts at Hanazono University (~2008), Kyoto University (~2008), and Bukkyo University (~2012).

Susumu Shimazono is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and later held positions at Sophia University.

Susumu Winston Nakamura (1908–1989) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing and served as a lecturer at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1942–1946) and UC Berkeley.

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Otani, Paris, and Kyoto universities, he studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin, and served as professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the universities of London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded and presided over the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and served as an education professor at Ontario Tech University.
